items.title: Éric Cantona: ‘If I regret something about the kung fu kick, it’s that I would love to kick him in another place’
items.summary: “I’m an angel and a demon,” Éric Cantona says intently during a gripping new documentary about his life on and off the football pitch. “And an angel or a demon, you love him or you hate him. I’m far from being the person with the greatest integrity. I’m far from being the person who always tells the
items.text:
“I’m an angel and a demon,” Éric Cantona says intently during a gripping new documentary about his life on and off the football pitch. “And an angel or a demon, you love him or you hate him. I’m far from being the person with the greatest integrity. I’m far from being the person who always tells the truth. I’m far from being the person who has never been hypocritical. Maybe I’m a good person, but I can also be a flower of evil. It’s the first time in my life I’ve realised this. I am a flower of evil, and I find it very beautiful.”
It’s hard to know what to expect from the only written interview pinned to the release of Cantona: Flower of Evil. Joel Cantona has warned that his famous brother will walk out at any mention of the enduring crisis surrounding Manchester United, whether it’s a question about Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival or the Glazer family’s ruinous ownership of the club.
I prepare for a possible meltdown because rare archive footage, which opens the documentary, captures a televised standoff between Cantona and a few French journalists. He objects to the fact that L’Équipe had described his kung fu kick against a Crystal Palace supporter in 1995 as “unforgivable”. After asking who is truly “unforgivable”, and highlighting the historical sins of the Catholic church, Cantona sneers: “I piss on the pope’s arse. Just as I piss on the arse of certain journalists … including you and you,” he says, pointing to two outraged writers.
Now, 30 years later, Cantona emerges in his home city of Marseille, wearing a natty trilby. Within minutes I can tell that the flower of evil is elsewhere because Cantona is in a generous mood. As he recalls that bitterly sensational clash with the French reporters he smiles: “I’m a good client for the journalists – and they are a good client for me to express myself. We play a bit like the cat and the mouse. Sometimes we have good relationships, sometimes a bad relationship. But it’s always interesting and exciting.”
This might be Cantona at his most angelic, stretching the truth about the supposed thrill of his journalistic encounters, but it’s fitting that the film starts with the 60-year-old quoting Charles Baudelaire, the 19th-century French poet who, in his Flowers of Evil collection, wrote: “I am the wound and the knife/I am the blow and the cheek/ … The victim and the executioner …”
Cantona’s brilliance and spite defined his troubled time at six French clubs between 1983 and 1992. He could have “disappeared” from football because, despite being France’s most gifted player, he had fallen out with the national manager. The young Cantona said: “I hope people realise Henri Michel is one of the most incompetent coaches in world football.”
Michel Platini, who replaced Michel, persuaded Cantona to end his fleeting retirement in 1992 by moving to England. As Cantona says: “I knew it will be my last chance … and it’s really in England where I regain this passion for football … it’s a rebirth.”
The documentary provides a compelling account of his turbulent love affair with English football – but ignores a strange prelude at Sheffield Wednesday. Cantona tells me this forgotten strand of his story with amused incredulity. “I arrived at Sheffield Wednesday and we played a friendly. We won 4-3 and I scored three goals. And then I waited to sign the contract. At the end of the week they said: ‘You have to spend one more week on trial.’ I said: ‘No. I leave.’”
Who managed Wednesday then? “Trevor Francis – who was a great player,” Cantona replies. “Howard Wilkinson heard about that and asked me to come to Leeds. I arrived in Leeds and then we became champions and it was a great time.”
That deceptively simple last sentence fails to capture the seismic impact Cantona had on English football and especially on Leeds, who won the league title for the first time in 18 years in 1992. “It was old-fashioned football,” Cantona says. “It was interesting. There was also, for me, the feeling of adding something different.”
Was it disheartening playing antiquated football? “No, because I played with wonderful players. We had a great midfield with Gary Speed, David Batty, Gary McAllister and Gordon Strachan. And quickly [the following season] I arrive at Manchester United with Alex Ferguson. The club had the Busby Babes. That was wonderful football. Manchester United has always been a club where winning in a good way is important.”
This should be the moment to ask Cantona about the contrast with the current moribund state of United but, rather than falling out over his refusal to discuss the club now, it’s enough to hear him in full flow. “This club always loved people with different personalities. They loved George Best, Brian McClair, [Norman] Whiteside, [Roy] Keane …”
Cantona was adored at Old Trafford, as he had been at Leeds before his shock departure to United for a mere £1m in November 1992. He also led United to their first Premier League title, in 1993, after a 26-year drought.
There are great clubs in Italy, Spain and Germany so could he have resurrected his career in one of these countries? Cantona shakes his head: “I love Italian football. I love Spanish football. I love Barcelona. But nothing can compare to English football and the fans, the way they sing and express themselves. It’s so powerful.”
Cantona remembers that, when he arrived in England, “in the street, nobody knew me. I felt free for the first time in my life. I could go have a drink somewhere, listen to some music and it was always peaceful.”
Ferguson recalls that he asked Guy Roux, the wise old manager who nurtured Cantona at his first club, Auxerre, how to harness his volatile talent. Roux offered two words: “Love him.”
Cantona nods: “I’m instinctive. If I feel bad I go. If I feel good, I try to create a relationship. And when I arrive in Manchester I see the ghosts of the past. I felt this very strong energy and I thought: ‘Maybe this is the place where I will have the opportunity to express myself.

Report from the Europa League game between Celta Vigo and Bournemouth at Estadio Abanca-Balaidos; Iago Aspas put home side in front before Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan struck to earn the Cherries a historic victory as Bournemouth extended their winning run to 10 matches in all competitions
Thursday 26 November 2026 20:05, UK
Bournemouth continued their magnificent run of form with a 2-1 victory against Celta Vigo, creating two bits of history in the process.
It was a club-record-extending 10th successive win for Bournemouth in all competitions, with the victory also marking the first time an English club have won their first five matches in major European competition.

Veteran former Liverpool striker Iago Aspas put the home side in front in style in the first half, before Bournemouth were reduced to 10 men when Bafode Diakite was sent off for a late challenge.
But Alvaro Rodriguez equalised early in the second half, with substitute Rayan coming on to score a late winner to give Bournemouth an unlikely win.
Bournemouth were fortunate not to go behind after 10 minutes, with an offside flag chalking off Pablo Duran's poke home from close-range.
But the Cherries fell behind 10 minutes later when record Celta Vigo goalscorer Aspas scored a screamer.
The 39-year-old had seen an overhead kick saved well by Michele Di Gregorio, but he picked up the ball on the right side of the area in the second phase of play, before cutting inside to curl past the goalkeeper and into the far corner off the post.
Things went from bad to worse for Bournemouth moment later when Diakite saw a yellow card upgraded to a red after a VAR check following a late challenge on Couhaib Driouech.
Tyler Adams replaced Justin Kluivert at half-time and the tactical switch drew an instant reward when Alvaro Rodriguez glanced home Amine Adli's cross to get Bournemouth back on level terms.
James Hill then drew a fine save from Ionut Radu - who is the only player ever to play for both clubs - before Di Gregorio was called into action at the other end to divert a long-range Aspas strike away.
But three Bournemouth substitutes combined for a late winner.
Adrien Truffert stole possession and broke before finding Marcus Tavernier the area. He laid the ball off for Rayan to sweep home and seal victory as Marco Rose's side made more history with a brilliant win at the Estadio Abanca-Balaidos.

items.title: Fifa staff asked to attend interviews as Infantino sell-off scheme investigated
items.summary:
A number of past and present Fifa employees have received letters requesting they attend interviews for a Congressional investigation into the global governing body sparked by the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal.
Letters were sent on Wednesday to a number of staff along with a handful of former empl
items.text:
A number of past and present Fifa employees have received letters requesting they attend interviews for a Congressional investigation into the global governing body sparked by the Fifa Forward Enterprise scandal.
Letters were sent on Wednesday to a number of staff along with a handful of former employees who held senior positions. They have been asked by Democrats on the House judiciary committee to give evidence as efforts gather pace to examine Gianni Infantino’s failed FFE scheme along with links between Fifa and the Trump administration.
Should recipients agree, the voluntary interviews could commence as soon as next week. They would be likely to take place under the whistleblower protection act or the victim and witness protection act, although the potential interviewees will seek legal advice before agreeing to take part.
The investigation’s gathering of momentum will increase pressure on Infantino, who could be among those subpoenaed to give evidence to the committee in January. The committee is controlled by Democrats after their success in the midterms and is likely to be chaired by Jamie Raskin, who warned in July that it would “have the tools we need to get answers, expose corruption, protect sports fans against exorbitant and fraudulent charges and block this attempt to turn world soccer into a global financial shakedown”.
The White House has previously dismissed similar allegations as politically motivated. Fifa did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Subpoenas could be issued to a range of individuals within Fifa, and in the organisation’s orbit, as soon as the second week of January. Those required to give evidence at a hearing could be required to disclose their knowledge of the FFE plan and other Fifa controversies, potentially handing over physical evidence.
Fifa confirmed on Thursday it had fallen victim to a criminal cyberattack carried out by a group that posed as staff members to steal personal and business data. A group called the Handsome Boy Hacking Club claimed responsibility for the breach, understood to have taken place on 11 November.
In a letter to the Fifa council dated 25 November, seen by the Guardian, the Fifa secretary general, Mattias Grafström, said the hack had “resulted in information being illegally obtained which included data relevant to the personal profiles of key officials including Fifa Council members attending Fifa tournaments and events”. Grafström wrote that Fifa had “taken mitigating and corrective steps” and told council members that they would be contacted individually where necessary.

items.text:
Referee being 'drunk' claims are 'entirely unfounded'
- Published
Claims that a referee was drunk during an Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League Two match are "entirely unfounded", officials say.
Syrian referee Hanna Hattab was replaced at half-time of the match between Iran's Gol Gohar and Al Jazira of the United Arab Emirates.
Reports claimed Gol Gohar staff accused the referee of being drunk following what has been described as some erratic decision-making in the first half.
Iranian news agency ISNA quoted one club official as saying: "The referee was not in a normal state," and suggesting they would not have played on had the referee not been removed.
Accusations of drunkenness were also widely shared on social media.
But Hattab, who is part of the AFC's elite refereeing group, has released a statement denying the allegation, saying he has been defamed and threatening legal action.
The fourth official took over for the second half, with Al Jazira winning the match.
Hattab said he will be "issuing an official statement that clarifies all the details and facts related to what happened".
Omani sports journalist Issa Said, who covers Asian competitions, claimed on social media that what happened to Hattab was "due to a drop in his blood sugar, which caused him to lose concentration and focus".
"He underwent a medical examination after the match and was not intoxicated, contrary to what has been circulating."
In their statement on the match, which was played in Asia's second tier continental competition, the Syrian Football Association backed Hattab.
"Following an assessment of his health, it has been confirmed - contrary to various claims circulating on social media - that the reports regarding his situation are entirely unfounded," they wrote.
"The Committee reiterates its unwavering support for him and is committed to thoroughly investigating all details and circumstances surrounding the incident."

items.text:
Why are winter rains forcing Palestinians in Gaza to flee again?
Israeli restrictions on humanitarian aid, damaged buildings and flooded tents leave displaced Palestinians vulnerable.
When heavy rain swept through az-Zawayda in central Gaza in early November, water rushed into Jaber al-Kaseeh’s tent, soaking his family’s mattresses and spoiling their food.
Al-Kaseeh, who fled Beit Lahiya in northern Gaza, told Al Jazeera that his camp had flooded three or four times the previous winter. Those floods had already driven many of his neighbours away.
About 1.36 million Palestinians, 65 percent of Gaza’s population, are living in tents and makeshift shelters, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).
The storm that began on the evening of November 6 flooded about 70,000 tents within 12 hours, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office. Preliminary UN estimates suggest it affected about 226,000 people, including more than 5,000 households left sleeping without shelter. About 600 households were forced to move again.
The rain also killed people. On November 8, a sand embankment collapsed onto tents at a displacement camp south of Deir el-Balah, killing five people, including children. OCHA reported that an infant drowned during the same storm and a nine-month-old baby died of hypothermia on November 13.
The Union of Gaza Strip Municipalities warned on Wednesday that about 1,000 camps and other shelter sites could flood this winter. The councils say 200,000 worn-out tents need replacing and more than 2,000 damaged buildings are at risk of collapse.
As Gaza enters its fourth winter since Israel launched its genocidal war in October 2023, we look at how Israeli restrictions on humanitarian aid, damaged buildings and flooded tents leave displaced Palestinians at greater risk.
Why can’t Palestinians move somewhere safer?
Israeli restrictions keep Palestinians from reaching large parts of Gaza, which leaves them fewer options to move to safer areas, according to OCHA. On November 17, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and the World Food Programme said Gaza’s population had been confined to less than 40 percent of the territory and that more than half of its 1,700 displacement sites were on flood-prone land.
The threat of further displacement persists. On Thursday, Israel Katz, the defence minister in Israel’s caretaker government, threatened a new offensive that would move one million Palestinians south if Hamas did not disarm. Writing on X, he called Hamas’s control over the remaining 30 percent of Gaza “an illusion”. He did not issue an evacuation order.
Damaged homes offer little refuge. About 82 percent of Gaza’s structures had been damaged or destroyed by mid-June, according to UN satellite analysis.
In Nuseirat, Nasser al-Hajj took his children to a neighbour’s home during the first November storm as debris fell from the ceiling of his flat, which an Israeli attack had damaged. “But where am I supposed to go? Rent is expensive, and a tent is not safe either,” he told Al Jazeera.
Why is Gaza so vulnerable to flooding?
Israel’s war has wrecked the drains and sewers that would normally carry rainwater away. In Gaza City, eight pumping stations and three main rainwater collection basins were out of service when the first storm hit, municipal spokesperson Hosni Muhanna said. Even under the best conditions, he said, the remaining network could handle no more than a fifth of the rainwater.
At Sheikh Radwan lagoon, one of the city’s main collection basins, the water rose by nearly 1.5 metres (five feet) during the storm, OCHA reported. Its pumping station is operating at less than 40 percent of its design capacity, the UN office added on Thursday.
In central Gaza, the councils are worried about water rising suddenly in Wadi Gaza and flooding al-Mughraqa and az-Zahra. Emergency services are overstretched: Gaza’s civil defence said it received 2,166 distress calls on November 7 but could send crews to only 218; most callers received advice by phone.
What are the health risks?
During the early November rains, the UN said crews used suction trucks to remove water mixed with sewage from 58 shelters. At the Patient’s Friends Benevolent Society Hospital in Gaza City, water flooded the basement that housed the children’s department, pharmacy and radiology services. Elsewhere, flooded roads kept patients and staff from reaching clinics.
Crowding poses a separate risk. Families in crowded tents have too little water to maintain basic hygiene, paediatrician Sharif Matar told Al Jazeera at Gaza City’s Rantisi Children’s Hospital.
The World Health Organization (WHO) recorded 692 suspected meningitis cases between October 1 and November 23, most of them among babies under a year old. Gaza’s Ministry of Health issued an epidemic alert on November 24 after recording 272 cases in October, compared with a usual monthly average of 30 to 50.
Why isn’t enough shelter aid reaching families?
On November 13, the UN’s humanitarian team said more than 150,000 tents bought by aid organisations and governments were waiting outside Gaza, most of them in Egypt’s El Arish. On Wednesday, the European Commission said tents were still waiting on trucks because Israel had not allowed them or the equipment needed to put them up to enter. Goods from Egypt are routed for inspection through the Karem Abu Salem crossing (called Kerem Shalom in Israel) rather than entering directly through Rafah. Israeli authorities also classify some shelter supplies as “dual-use”, which limits how much aid groups can bring in.
COGAT, the Israeli military body that coordinates aid, said on Monday that nearly 100,000 tents had entered Gaza under its winter programme. It said it had approved more than 67,000 tents and other winter supplies that had yet to be brought in. Inside Gaza, shelter agencies have fewer than 6,500 tents in stock, the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) said on Wednesday.

After a Supreme Court ruling against it, the Trump administration had tried a narrower set of restrictions.
A United States federal judge has blocked an attempt by President Donald Trump’s administration to deny birthright c
items.text:
Judge strikes down Trump’s latest restrictions on US birthright citizenship
After a Supreme Court ruling against it, the Trump administration had tried a narrower set of restrictions.
A United States federal judge has blocked an attempt by President Donald Trump’s administration to deny birthright citizenship to certain categories of US-born children whose parents it argued were not subject to US jurisdiction.
In a ruling issued on Wednesday, District Court Judge Christopher Cooper said those children were still under US jurisdiction and thus were guaranteed citizenship under the US Constitution.
“The president cannot carve out new exceptions to birthright citizenship for children born within the United States and subject to its laws,” Cooper said in the order.
Another court in Maryland had also blocked the same policy by the Trump administration in a September ruling, issuing a preliminary injunction at the time.
The new ruling is another blow to Trump’s campaign to end birthright citizenship for children whose parents were not American citizens or legal permanent residents at their birth.
The Trump administration has argued that the US Constitution’s 14th Amendment – which says all “persons born or naturalised in the United States, and subject to the jurisdiction thereof, are citizens of the United States” – was not meant to apply to parents who were not permanently living in the country.
The latest lawsuit was brought by several rights groups on behalf of children who would be affected by Trump’s executive orders in August that targeted birthright citizenship.
US Supreme Court precedent
The case was heard after the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s initial order on birthright citizenship in June, ruling that the lawmakers who drafted the 14th Amendment knew how broad its language was and did not limit it in the way the president was trying to.
Trump, who had taken the rare step of personally attending arguments at the Supreme Court in that case, has said he is unhappy with the June ruling.
In it, the Supreme Court cited a previous case it had considered in 1898 brought by a US-born Chinese American who was being denied citizenship. Wong Kim Ark’s parents had left the US for their native China after he was born, and when Wong returned as an adult, he was denied entry with officials saying he was not considered a citizen.
Soon after the Supreme Court’s ruling, Trump tried to again restrict birthright citizenship with a new order taking aim at “birth tourism”, in which women travel to the US to give birth so their children can obtain automatic citizenship. The order also targeted children whose parents work for foreign governments or international organizations but lack diplomatic immunity and those who have a parent who is classified as an “alien enemy”.
The president “needs to accept that birthright citizenship is the law of the land”, said Cody Wofsy, a lawyer with the American Civil Liberties Union, one of the groups representing plaintiffs in the latest case. “The Supreme Court has twice rejected efforts to gut birthright citizenship, in 1898 and again earlier this year. Third time is not the charm.”
White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said in a statement that the court’s decision was “just another ruling from an activist judge” and Trump’s order had been “consistent with the holdings and analysis set forth by the Supreme Court”.
In a study last year, the Migration Policy Institute estimated that about 255,000 babies a year who were born to parents who were unauthorised immigrants or on temporary visas and thus subject to Trump’s initial executive order would be denied citizenship if the Supreme Court had upheld that policy.
Roots in the US Civil War era
The 14th Amendment, ratified in 1868 after the US Civil War, automatically made those born to previously enslaved people citizens of the country. Its broad language, though, also extended to others born in the country, an interpretation US courts have said was in line with English traditions preceding the founding of the United States.
Indigenous people were seen as an exception to that provision because they enjoyed some legal autonomy, and it was not until 1924 that the US Congress passed a law granting them citizenship.
Since taking office, Trump has set out a broad agenda to restrict immigration, restricting visas and political asylum for much of the world and directing federal law enforcement agencies to institute a national crackdown on allegedly undocumented immigrants.
Along with trying to restrict who is granted birthright citizenship, the Trump administration has also stepped up lawsuits to strip already naturalised people of their status if they committed major crimes and concealed that history from authorities.

Psychiatric care under scrutiny after abuse scandals in Croatia and Bosnia
Persistent failures in psychiatric care have been exposed, including staff shortages, inadequate training and weak oversight.
Thousands gathered in Zagreb’s Ban Josip Jelacic Square on Saturday, carrying white pillows marked with bloody handprints.
The symbolic protest was held in memory of 32-year-old Kristian Josip Peris, who died at the Sveti Ivan Psychiatric Clinic in the Croatian capital after medical staff allegedly tried to restrain him by placing a pillow over his face, according to publicly released security camera footage.
Several days later, footage from the psychiatric ward of a public hospital in the city of Zenica, in neighbouring Bosnia and Herzegovina, sparked public outrage. The video showed medical staff physically assaulting a patient.
The two cases in neighbouring countries led to the arrest of at least 13 healthcare workers, the resignations of the heads of the psychiatric institutions involved, and a wave of public anger.
But they also raised a broader question: What happens behind the closed doors of institutions meant to protect some of society’s most vulnerable people?
These are not the first cases to have shocked the region.
Bosnia and Herzegovina still remembers the Pazaric institutional abuse scandal, involving a small settlement located about 30km (18.6 miles) from the capital, Sarajevo, where residents of a state institution for children and young people with additional needs were tied to radiators and subjected to physical abuse.
Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, once part of the same country, Yugoslavia, have spent the past three decades trying to bring their healthcare systems and societies closer to European standards.
Croatia joined the European Union in 2013, while Bosnia and Herzegovina is forging its own path towards membership.
Unlike in some Western countries, where private healthcare providers play a significant role in mental health services, psychiatric inpatient care in Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia is predominantly provided through public healthcare institutions.
Although private providers also operate in the region, public institutions remain central to the provision of specialised psychiatric hospital care.
This makes the role of public authorities particularly important, not only in ensuring access to treatment but also in supervising institutions, maintaining adequate staffing levels and protecting patients’ rights.
‘Problem lies in consistently following those protocols’
Edin Bjelosevic, a neuropsychiatrist and university professor from Zenica, said the legal frameworks in countries that emerged from the breakup of Yugoslavia largely reflect contemporary standards for treating people with mental health conditions.
“The problem lies in consistently following those protocols, rather than in access to modern treatments and procedures,” Bjelosevic told Al Jazeera.
According to Eurostat, the EU’s statistical office, about 96,000 psychiatrists were working across 25 member countries in 2024. Germany had the highest number relative to its population, with 29 psychiatrists per 100,000 people. Croatia recorded 19.1, above the European average, while Serbia had 12.4 psychiatrists per 100,000 people.
Bosnia and Herzegovina, according to World Health Organization (WHO) data from 2020, had just 9.48 psychiatrists per 100,000 people. More recent comparable figures for the country are not available.
Differences are also evident in the number of psychiatric hospital beds. Croatia had 93 beds per 100,000 people, compared with the European average of 71. Serbia recorded 82, while Bosnia and Herzegovina, with 40 beds per 100,000 people, was significantly below the average.
Eurostat and WHO figures may differ from data published by national statistical agencies.
However, the number of psychiatrists and hospital beds alone does not provide a complete picture of the quality of care, patient safety or the working conditions of healthcare professionals.
Staff shortages increase risks
In its 2024-2025 report, Croatia’s Ombudswoman called on the Ministry of Health to improve the functioning of psychiatric institutions. Among the recommendations was better training for medical staff in the use of coercive measures involving people with mental health conditions.
Coercive measures are used in psychiatric institutions around the world. They involve temporarily restricting a patient’s freedom of movement to prevent an immediate risk of harm to themselves or others. However, they are not intended as a routine means of controlling patients, but as a last resort when other approaches have failed.
Following Peris’s death, Croatia’s Ministry of Health identified shortcomings at the clinic, ordering five corrective measures.
The inspection found faults in staff training and staffing levels, alongside problems with the supervision of patients subjected to coercive measures, medical record-keeping and reporting procedures following the patient’s death.
Staffing levels did not meet the required standards, with a shortage of one physiotherapist and one nursing assistant. The ministry also found faults in the scope and quality of staff training on managing patients in crisis situations.
Health Minister Irena Hrstic said four of the five corrective measures were to take effect immediately, while the clinic was given 60 days to bring its staffing levels into line with the required standards.
The findings highlighted concerns that go beyond the conduct of individual healthcare workers, raising questions about staffing, training and institutional oversight in psychiatric care.
Abdulah Kucukalic, a neuropsychiatrist from Sarajevo, said psychiatric institutions across the region share a common problem: a shortage of non-medical personnel specifically trained to deal safely with patients experiencing acute psychiatric crises.

Tonda Eckert: Southampton boss wants to close the chapter on 'Spygate' ahead of Middlesbrough reunion
Tonda Eckert speaks to Sky Sports News reporter Mark McAdam about 'Spygate' fallout, their points deduction and reunion with Middlesbrough. Watch Southampton vs Middlesbrough live on Sky Sports Foot
items.text:
Tonda Eckert: Southampton boss wants to close the chapter on 'Spygate' ahead of Middlesbrough reunion
Tonda Eckert speaks to Sky Sports News reporter Mark McAdam about 'Spygate' fallout, their points deduction and reunion with Middlesbrough. Watch Southampton vs Middlesbrough live on Sky Sports Football from 7.30pm on Friday night; kick-off 8pm.
Thursday 26 November 2026 19:28, UK
"I think we've experienced a little bit more in the last 12 months than normal."
It may be the understatement of the century, but it's not a huge surprise considering Tonda Eckert is a relatively understated man.
The storm of 'Spygate' is over, but the aftershock is still being felt. Southampton are sixth in the table, seven points behind leaders Middlesbrough ahead of their reunion on Friday night - live on Sky Sports.
Were it not for the four-point deduction, the gap would be smaller. Were it not for the entire controversy, the Saints would possibly be in the Premier League right now.

- Got Sky? Watch EFL games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream EFL games with no contract📺
Eckert knows he broke the rules, and is thankful for the club and the support-base for backing him. Something that wouldn't have been easy after the ignominy of being kicked out of the play-offs.
"There have been some points, especially over the summer, where I think the club has made a commitment that not many clubs would have made," he admits.
"I'm very grateful, first of all, for the opportunity to step up in the first place, but also for the support over the summer. Obviously, that goes from everyone in the building to our supporters.
"This summer has been the biggest test we can possibly have in terms of the relationship between a football club and a fan base, and a manager and a fan base. I think the supporters have been great. It's been a tough period for them.
"Towards the end of last season, it was difficult to process for everyone because of the process we used. I would have wanted to address the supporters a little earlier, so it took almost two weeks before I got to speak to them.
"From there on, I think the commitment has been very clear. It started with the football club and some players who committed to the project.
"You could just sense, the closer we got to the season, that everyone wanted to leave that behind and show what we are about as a football club and how much joy we bring when we go on the pitch. We felt that throughout the summer and on the first day of training.
"To come out of that situation with new strength just shows what this football club is about. Now it's for us to look forward and make sure that we continue to do that.
"There was still some uncertainty for the first block of games, and you just need to find a way, for me and obviously for everyone else in the football club, to put that to the side. As soon as the season starts, you need to perform.
"Then, obviously, to close that chapter finally, we needed a decision from the club. I think that's helped us to close that chapter."
The uncertainty came from the FA investigation, which wasn't resolved until October. In the end he was given a fine and a suspended six-week ban.
"Obviously, it's never easy to work on a daily basis if you have some uncertainty, and that's not just for me," he says. "I think it's the same for everyone at the football club.
"But I think we found a way, even in the first block of games, to perform. There's always something going on in football, sometimes a little bit bigger and sometimes not as big, but you need to push that to the side and make sure you find a way to perform.
"Once the decision came, I think it was important for everyone that we could finally close that."
For Eckert and Southampton it is just about points on the board, now. Trying to make up the deficit they were dealt at the start of the season.
"Obviously, if you could choose, no one would choose to start the season on minus four points," he says. "That's what it is. I think we are strong enough to make our way forward in the table.
"You shouldn't underestimate us coming from behind. We've shown that we are able to chase teams down, and that's the job for this year.
"It's been important for us to get some points on the board early in the season. We are still not where we want to be towards the end, so we need to make sure we continue."
Last week, Southampton handed Eckert, still just 33, a contract extension until 2029. They clearly feel he is their man to get them back to where they want to be.
"I think we've always been very open with our ambitions," he says. "There's no point in hiding that.
"I think the conditions are there to go up. It's never easy, but it's for us now to finish the job."

items.text:
Reporters Without Borders demands suspension of controversial French TV channel CNews
Paris-based international press freedom group Reporters Without Borders (RSF) on Thursday called on France's media regulator Arcom to suspend right-wing channel CNews for one month over its failure to uphold pluralism. The news channel owned by conservative billionaire Vincent Bolloré condemned the call for its suspension.
Reporters Without Borders (RSF) on Thursday demanded a one-month suspension of French news channel CNews over allegedly biased coverage in favour of the far right ahead of elections next year.
The Paris-based international press freedom group, which usually campaigns for imprisoned journalists and against censorship around the world, said that it had written to France's media regulator Arcom to urge action against CNews.
Read moreFrench prosecutors open hate speech probe into polarising news channel CNews
It called for a one-month suspension, with RSF director general Thibaut Bruttin saying "there is a danger for democracy that is becoming more evident as we get closer to the presidential election".
Arcom told AFP that it was investigating and suspected a "breach" of its rules governing radio and TV channels that oblige news bosses to offer a variety of political points of view.
CNews, owned by the conservative billionaire Vincent Bolloré, is seen by its critics as a partisan far-right outlet.
Read moreHow Bolloré, the ‘French Murdoch’, carried Le Pen’s far right to the brink of power
Its fans believe it has helped address alleged left-wing bias in the media and appreciate its focus on crime and immigration.
"How can an organisation (RSF) whose mission historically is to defend press freedom around the world today even contemplate calling for the closure, for one month, of France's leading news channel, and moreover just a few months before the presidential election?" the channel said in a statement.
"CNews condemns Reporters Without Borders' relentless campaign against it," the company added.
CNews has been handed 12 warnings and 11 fines from the regulator, totalling €830,000 ($911,000) since its creation in 2017, according to RSF research.
"Reporters Without Borders defends press freedom. Press freedom also means being able to distinguish between what amounts to brainwashing and what is genuine, free and independent journalism," Bruttin said.
Investigations
Investigators from RSF watched 61 hours of three of the most-watched shows on the channel, concluding that "immigration, insecurity, Islamism, identity issues, criticism of the left and the public media" accounted for two-thirds of the topics debated.
In an investigation last year, RSF found that CNews used its overnight slots, when few people watch, to broadcast more left-leaning content to satisfy the regulatory demands for balanced programming.
It has regularly urged Arcom to take firmer action against CNews since 2021.
Far-right leader Marine Le Pen is currently leading in the polls ahead of the two-round French presidential election next year, on April 18 and May 2.
(FRANCE 24 with AFP)

items.title: Fifa confirms cyber-attack exposed ‘personal and business information’
items.summary:
Fifa confirmed that hackers gained access to a “limited set of personal and business information” in a cyber-attack, amid heightened concern over digital vulnerabilities of leading organizations and institutions.
The global soccer governing body said it “condemns in the strongest possible terms the
items.text:
Fifa confirmed that hackers gained access to a “limited set of personal and business information” in a cyber-attack, amid heightened concern over digital vulnerabilities of leading organizations and institutions.
The global soccer governing body said it “condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data”, in a statement to the Associated Press on Thursday. “Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned.”
Last week, a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted a screenshot on X of what it claimed were Fifa files. The post has since then been removed after the account was suspended from X.
The Fifa cyber-attack is the latest high-profile digital disruption to hit a major organization in recent weeks.
Microsoft experienced a widespread outage earlier this month that caused disruption to millions of users, organizations and businesses across the globe. The company said the outage was a “technical issue” not related to cyber-attacks or AI agents.
The following day, the US experienced an unprecedented nationwide disruption to air travel that prompted a “ground stop” order to be issued by the US Federal Aviation Administration, which cited “communication issues” impacting air traffic control centers.
Markwayne Mullin, the homeland security secretary, later said in a news conference that preliminary investigations into the stoppage did not indicate that it was tied to a “nefarious attack”.
Three days later, customers reported service outages and difficulty accessing their online accounts at several major US banks and the money transfer service Zelle after a technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused ripple effects throughout the financial system.
Such disruptions have intensified fear and concerns about the advancement of artificial intelligence, and the potential risks, even though there is no direct evidence that AI directly sparked the issues.
ESPN reported that unnamed sources said the Fifa hack accounted for less than 0.1% of data held by the organization, an that the breach was not a result of systems or technology failure on Fifa’s part, with hackers said to have gained access by impersonating staff.
As of now, it has not been shared when the cyber-attack took place, or the precise nature of the hacked information.
“FIFA is working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement,” the organization said its statement sent to the Associated Press.
The cyber-attack comes as Gianni Infantino, Fifa’s president, is under scrutiny for a proposal to sell chunks of the World Cup to private investors.
Infantino admitted the project “has created divisions of a nature that are no longer in the interest of the objective”, amid widespread anger globally.
The plan has caused tensions within football around the world, leading Uefa to threaten a boycott of future Fifa tournaments if it was not shelved.
Uefa and other confederations have stepped up their search for candidates to run against Infantino in next year’s Fifa election, in which he had been expected to comfortably win a fourth term.

Ian Copestake writes: “I was surprised at how happy I felt seeing Iago Aspas again! As a fan of one of his very few other clubs, it did not work out for him at Liverpool. But there he is doing goals!”
Celta Vigo 1-1 Bournemouth: In the early kick-off, Bournemouth are level in northern Spain after Rodriguez cancelled out Iago Aspas’ opener. Unfortunately for the Cherries they are a man light after Diakite was dismissed.
Who better than Ed Aarons to run you through what is going on at Crystal Palace?
Simon Teesdale could not help feeling mixed emotions when his beloved Crystal Palace won the Conference League in Leipzig in May. He started going to Selhurst Park with his father in the 1980s, became a season-ticket holder in the 1990s and has watched with pride as the club established itself as a permanent fixture in the Premier League over the past 14 years. Palace finally secured a major trophy in the 2025 FA Cup final – an experience Teesdale remembers as “one of the best days of my life” – and followed that up by winning the Conference League but he decided in August not to renew his season ticket.
“Something happened between the FA Cup win and today that changed me,” he wrote in an emotional article published last month on his website. “Tipped me over the edge. Actually, it’s fairer to say that something accelerated in that period of time. The seeds were sown years ago.”
Thomas Frank has the opportunity to get his Crystal Palace tenure up and running but faces a tough task against Real Sociedad. The Dane is not long in the role but knows he needs to get the backing of the Selhurst Park faithful, which means notching points on the both ASAP, regardless of the competition.
Sunderland host Jagiellonia Białystok and win would move them into double figures after five games played. Considering the difficulties they have endured domestically, such a result would be a fine boost to morale. Dinamo Zagreb showed them up at the Stadium of Light, so the hosts will need to be on guard to avoid a repeat.

items.title: Leclerc denies having 'No 1 clause' in Ferrari contract
items.summary:
Charles Leclerc denies presence of 'No 1 driver' clause in Ferrari contract as he and Lewis Hamilton hold 'good discussions' after collision
Charles Leclerc was penalised by the stewards and criticised by Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur after causing a collision with Lewis Hamilton in Las Vegas; watch
items.text:
Charles Leclerc denies presence of 'No 1 driver' clause in Ferrari contract as he and Lewis Hamilton hold 'good discussions' after collision
Charles Leclerc was penalised by the stewards and criticised by Ferrari boss Frederic Vasseur after causing a collision with Lewis Hamilton in Las Vegas; watch the Qatar GP on Sky Sports F1 this weekend, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday
Thursday 26 November 2026 18:13, UK
Charles Leclerc has strongly denied suggestions he has a No 1 driver clause in his Ferrari contract.
The Monegasque, who has been with the team since 2019 and signed an extended deal earlier this year, was speaking ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix as both he and Lewis Hamilton faced the media again four days on from their latest clash at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty by the stewards for causing a collision as he attempted to overtake Hamilton for sixth place in Las Vegas, with the incident also earning him severe criticism from Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur.

The Las Vegas collision came just three weeks after a fierce battle between the team-mates - with Hamilton running first and Leclerc second - on the opening lap in Mexico City cost Ferrari a likely one-two, with clear-the-air discussions required after Red Bull's Max Verstappen won that race.
Vasseur has hitherto played down the need to impose strict, pre-determined rules of engagement on his drivers to avoid future repeats. There had subsequently been speculation that, perhaps, there were contractual reasons on Leclerc's side preventing the team from formally intervening in this way.
But offered the chance on Thursday to respond to claims about a so-called 'No 1 driver' clause in his deal, Leclerc said: "I normally never disclose what I have in my contract, but I think this one is an important one to speak about.
"And I absolutely have zero clause that says that in my contract.
"It's never something that I was interested in and never something that I personally wanted."
"At the end of the day, we are two very strong drivers that want to finish one ahead of the other. Unfortunately, it finished recently, whether it's in here or Monza or Mexico.
"There's been a bit too many events of those lately and we need to find a solution as a team to make sure that these kind of things don't happen again."
Leclerc bore the brunt of Vasseur's post-race criticism last Sunday and, asked if he agreed with the Frenchman that the crash with Hamilton had indeed been "unacceptable", replied: "That it is unacceptable, of course.
"As a team, we cannot afford to clash between team-mates and I think that is very clear for everyone. For the clash in particular of Las Vegas, as I said, I took responsibility.
"I think there's just tension around, that we just need to dissipate and make sure that we look at more positive days in the future. That's all I'm looking for. But yeah, I do agree. It's unacceptable that both Ferrari clash together, of course."
Hamilton: Charles and I are still free to race
Vasseur had promised further talks with his drivers following the race in Vegas, having insisted the clashes between the pair "cannot continue".
The drivers confirmed talks had taken place, with both the team principal and among themselves, with Hamilton saying they had been "good discussions" and "positive".
Neither driver said they would elaborate on what was discussed, with Leclerc stating in the official FIA news conference that he "cannot disclose" what possible "solutions" were agreed to avoid future repeats or whether there were any measures in place already for the final two rounds of this season.
But Hamilton confirmed they remained free to race each other.
"We're still free to race, and I think that's the ultimate goal of being here. We race, right?" said Hamilton.
"Of course, we don't want what happened last week to ever happen, so we communicate. Charles and I had a good sit down earlier on and had our chat, and I I think moving forwards we can be fine.
"We literally focus on racing hard and fair, and continue to try and enjoy it. We do enjoy racing together, and we do have a really good relationship.
"It's obviously intense in the background, well on the outside, it seems a lot more intense than it really is inside."
Hamilton has previously called for the team to adopt clearer guidelines on how he and Leclerc are able to race each other but, speaking on Thursday, said it was Vasseur's final call to make.
"That's for Fred to decide ultimately," he said. "I made my point clear already about them.
"So yeah, there's not really much more to say on it really. I said my piece before and and my point hasn't really changed."

items.text:
Calvert-Lewin signs new Leeds deal until 2029
- Published
Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract to stay with Leeds United until 2029.
The former Everton striker, 29, has five goals and one assist so far in the Premier League this season, with Daniel Farke's side sitting 11th in the table.
Confirmation of Calvert-Lewin's deal follows speculation about his future at the club, with reports that he was interesting Manchester United.
Calvert-Lewin scored 15 goals across all competitions during his first season at Elland Road after joining in August 2025, and the form earned him an England recall in March.
He was also called up by Thomas Tuchel this autumn and came off the bench in England's wins against Czech Republic and Spain.
He scored a penalty and had an assist in Leeds' 4-1 thrashing of Chelsea on Saturday.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new deal until the summer of 2029 at Leeds; the striker joined the club in 2025 from Everton; he has scored six goals in all competitions this season; his form earned him a reca
items.text:
Dominic Calvert-Lewis: Leeds striker signs new deal until 2029 with Premier League club
Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new deal until the summer of 2029 at Leeds; the striker joined the club in 2025 from Everton; he has scored six goals in all competitions this season; his form earned him a recall to the England squad
Thursday 26 November 2026 17:28, UK
Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new deal at Leeds, keeping him at the club until the summer of 2029.
Sky Sports News has been reporting that he was expected to commit his future to the club, which has now been confirmed.
Manchester United had shown interest in the 29-year-old.
Calvert-Lewin joined Leeds on a free transfer in the summer of 2025 after leaving Everton. He scored 15 goals across all competitions last season, and has scored six this season. He scored in a 4-1 win against Chelsea on Saturday.
Since he joined Leeds, Calvert-Lewin is the highest-scoring Englishman in the Premier League (19) - three ahead of his next closest countrymen, Morgan Gibbs-White and Ollie Watkins.
His form for Leeds saw him return to the England set-up in March, and he also featured in the September/October and November squads. Calvert-Lewin was not selected for the World Cup.

Ao Tanaka is also close to signing a new contract with Leeds, Sky Sports News understands.
The midfielder is understood to have agreed terms on a deal that will keep him at Elland Road until 2029. The 28-year-old's current contract was due to expire in the summer of 2028.
Tanaka has grown to become a key figure in Daniel Farke's side this season, starting in nine of Leeds' 11 Premier League matches. They have lost just 10 of the 66 games Tanaka has started since then.
Calvert-Lewin follows in the footsteps of Ethan Ampadu, Joe Rodon, Jayden Bogle and Brenden Aaronson, who all signed new deals in the summer. Leeds are also reportedly set to trigger Lukas Nmecha's one-year extension.
Leeds are seventh in the Premier League, four points from the Champions League places. They face Coventry next in the league on Saturday.
Farke not drawn on own future
Ahead of the weekend's match, Daniel Farke has refused to shed any more light on his own new contract talks. He signed a four-year contract when appointed in 2023 and that is set to expire at the end of the season.
He was reported to have parted company with his agent in October while reaching an agreement with Leeds in principle to extend his contract until 2029.
Farke said: "I'm the manager of Leeds United. I sign players. I don't sign managers. Since I've been here, I fell in love with the people here, and I fell in love with the club.
"And the only thing I care for is our supporters because they had to suffer really for such a long time. I want to bring success to them. I care for the players, I care for the staff and this is the way I work.
"I think this is also the reason I don't like to talk about my contract at all because I have to lead the people here.
"I'm a leader of men and women at this club and and no one wants a leader who talks about his future, about himself, or whatever. And this also not my style."

Traditional ad blockers can get detected by YouTube's anti-adblock system ("Ad blockers are not allowed here"), and the skip button takes a few seconds to appear. You sit there, hostage.
Reload the page. That's it. Two reloads and the ad is gone. Every time.
🎯 YouTube Ad Punisher automates this: the moment an ad appears, it captures your exact playback timestamp, reloads the page, and YouTube auto-seeks back to where you were. No ads. No waiting. No skip button hunting.
- Auto escape: after 3 reloads, the extension automatically switches to a helper tab for 4 seconds (George's discovery, now automated), then switches back. No manual tab switching needed.
- Ads keep coming after reload? Switch to another tab for a few seconds, then switch back. Chrome throttles background tabs, which lets the ad state settle — George discovered this works every time.
- Incognito: see the Incognito section above.
Ad detected → Capture timestamp → Reload page → Auto-seek to timestamp → Resume
                    ↓ (if 3 reloads fail)
              Redirect to yout-ube.com (ad-free mirror, no looping)
- Reload (primary) — reloads the page 1-3 times. YouTube re-evaluates ad serving on each reload; after 1-2 cycles the ad slot is empty and the video plays clean. Timestamp is preserved via &t=Xs URL param + JS seek.
- yout-ube.com redirect (fallback) — if reloads don't clear the ad after 3 attempts, redirects to yout-ube.com (an ad-free YouTube mirror). The URL includes &loop=0 to prevent the infinite replay issue that the mirror has by default.
- Detect — watches for .ad-showing class, skip buttons, and ad overlays (every 500ms + MutationObserver)
- Capture — grabs video.currentTime and saves it to sessionStorage
- Reload — location.replace() with &t=Xs in the URL
- Restore — YouTube auto-seeks to the timestamp; playback resumes
- Cooldown — 3-second guard prevents reload loops
- ✅ Zero ads — reloads until the ad is gone (usually 1-2 cycles)
- ✅ Timestamp preserved — never lose your place in the video
- ✅ Live streams — plain reload (no timestamp to preserve)
- ✅ Ad history database — every ad logged with advertiser, duration, skip text, video, and timestamp
- ✅ Export — JSON or CSV download of all collected ad data
- ✅ Popup viewer — click the extension icon to see stats, top advertisers, and full history
- ✅ No permissions abuse — only storage and tabs, only on YouTube domains
- Clone the repo:
git clone https://github.com/antonpictures/youtube-punisher.git
- Open chrome://extensions
- Enable Developer mode (top right)
- Click Load unpacked → select the youtube-punisher folder
- Done — activates on all YouTube pages automatically. ✅ Tested
Safari blocks ad-hoc signed extensions from auto-injecting into YouTube. As a workaround, use the JS overlay + AppleScript watcher (yt-ad-watch.sh):
- In Safari, enable: Safari → Settings → Advanced → Show Develop menu in menu bar
- In Safari (on a YouTube page), run ./yt-ad-watch.sh in Terminal
- When an ad appears, the watcher detects it via MutationObserver (event-driven in the page), reloads with &t=Xs, and the MutationObserver re-detects on the next page load
Note: This is best-effort. Chrome is fully reliable; Safari works but may need manual testing.
- Download the latest release from Releases
- Unzip and follow Option A steps 2–5
Every ad YouTube serves you is recorded:
Export as JSON or CSV from the popup. Data stays local — nothing is sent anywhere.
YouTube's ad system serves ads as part of the page load. When you reload, YouTube re-evaluates whether to serve an ad based on your session state. After 1-2 reloads, the ad slot is typically empty and the video plays directly. This is a client-side, zero-cost workaround — no filter lists, no network blocking, no detection by YouTube's anti-adblock system.
If millions of users did this, each reload = a full page load = server request. YouTube would see a spike in page loads but a drop in ad impressions. It's not a DDoS (no amplification, no botnet), but it's a passive protest: every reload is a vote that says "I will not watch your ad." The ad revenue model breaks when reloads are cheaper than ad views.
"Every reload is a vote: I will not watch your ad." — George Anton, creator
Best combo: uBlock Origin (blocks most ads) + 🎯 YouTube Ad Punisher (catches the ones that slip through and logs them) + SponsorBlock (skips sponsor reads). They don't conflict.
- YouTube changes DOM class names periodically — if ads aren't detected, check the console for [YT-AdReloader] logs
- Some ads (mid-roll on live streams) can't preserve position — plain reload
- YouTube's "Premium" upsell interstitials may need a second reload cycle (handled by cooldown)
MIT — do whatever you want with it.
Built with Alice (SIFTA) for George Anton.
"If millions installed this, YouTube would feel every reload." 🐜

The 28-year-old will miss the Women's World Cup next summer and is banned from all football activity until after 7 Octo
items.text:
Germany's Freigang banned over drugs test issues
- Published
Germany international Laura Freigang has been suspended from football for 16 months over issues with three drugs tests.
The 28-year-old will miss the Women's World Cup next summer and is banned from all football activity until after 7 October 2027.
The 16-month suspension begins from the date of notification by the German Football Association (DFB), which took place in June.
The World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada), the National Anti-Doping Agency (Nada), DFB and Freigang reached a dispute resolution agreement.
The dispute said Entracht Frankfurt forward Freigang committed three reporting and/or testing failures between 11 March 2025 and 23 February 2026.
Freigang can return to training two months prior to the end of the suspension period but cannot play matches until after 7 October.
All personal records of appearances, goals, assists or other statistics from 23 February 2026 are nullified, though Frankfurt's results are unaffected.
This season Freigang has scored six goals and provided two assists in 11 starts in the Frauen-Bundesliga.
Since joining the club in 2020, the striker has scored 107 goals in 187 appearances and was in the Germany squad for October's friendly victories over Australia and Japan.
In a club statement, external, Franfurt said they will "begin discussions shortly to determine the terms of her future employment relationship".
Freigang's current contract is due to expire on 30 June 2027.
Frankfurt's director of women's football Katharina Kiel said: "The agreement now reached provides clarity and planning security in a process unprecedented for Eintracht Frankfurt - for us as a club, but above all for Laura.
"The way she and the team have handled the situation in recent months, and how Laura personally led by example with her performance on the pitch during a very difficult time, deserves the highest recognition.
"The identified shortcomings, despite the agreement to settle the dispute, have resulted in a suspension, which means the loss of a key player."

Phil 'The Power' Taylor and Adrian Lewis suffered five losses from five matches for England at Thursday's Modus Super Series International Pairs Tournament in Portsmouth.
Taylor, now 66, retired from the competitive circuit in 2018, five years after claiming his 16th and final world title. However, the 16-time world champion returned to action to partner his long-time friend Lewis for the tournament.
Their opening match on Thursday saw them face Scotland's John Henderson and Robert Thornton, with the England pair suffering a narrow 4-3 defeat.
Things failed to improve in their second outing, as Taylor and Lewis were beaten 4-2 by Sweden's Andreas Harrysson and Anton Ostlund.

- Published
Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso says defender Wesley Fofana has apologised for a controversial interview he gave on YouTube.
Fofana has been criticised for comments he made in the interview with YouTuber Zach Nani in which he appeared to joke about h
items.text:
Fofana has apologised for interview - Alonso
- Published
Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso says defender Wesley Fofana has apologised for a controversial interview he gave on YouTube.
Fofana has been criticised for comments he made in the interview with YouTuber Zach Nani in which he appeared to joke about his penalty miss in a Carabao Cup shootout defeat at Liverpool.
He did not have permission to hold the two-hour interview, which was aired after Chelsea's humiliating 4-1 defeat at home to rivals Leeds on Saturday, but Alonso said the matter was now "closed".
"It was unfortunate. He has apologised. He knows it was not right, the moment, it was not right, the content," said the Blues boss, who was speaking before Friday's Premier League match at Nottingham Forest.
"We are here to take things seriously. He's said it will not be repeated. We don't want these kind of things and they won't be repeated."
Alonso refused to confirm whether Fofana had been punished by the club, but said "we have addressed that with him."
Fofana's comments followed criticism from fans of his performances this season, including in last weekend's humiliation at the hands of historic rivals Leeds.
But interviewer Nani defended Fofana against the backlash, saying: "People can clearly see he wasn't happy. He admits he didn't play well and says he needs to improve."
The interviewer also defended Fofana's explanation for putting himself forward to take a penalty against Liverpool, saying the defender believed it was his responsibility as one of the senior players on the pitch.
The 25-year-old France defender has often struggled for form and fitness since completing a £70m move from Leicester City in August 2022.
He has made 81 appearances for the club in four years, but has played nine times under new manager Alonso this season.
In that time Chelsea have struggled with defensive frailty, conceding 20 goals in their 11 Premier League games.
They are eighth in the table after falling to a third defeat in their last four league matches.

items.title: As Anthropic IPOs, Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue
items.summary:
It should have been impossible for “Grand Theft Auto VI” (GTA VI) to live up to the hype. Fans waited 13 years for the newest installment in the crime-adventure franchise, and Rockstar Games exceeded even those inconceivable expectations when the game finally came out last week.
GTA VI launched as t
items.text:
It should have been impossible for “Grand Theft Auto VI” (GTA VI) to live up to the hype. Fans waited 13 years for the newest installment in the crime-adventure franchise, and Rockstar Games exceeded even those inconceivable expectations when the game finally came out last week.
GTA VI launched as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and made $3.79 billion on release day to mark what could be the biggest entertainment event ever – more massive than “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.9 billion) or Taylor Swift’s Eras tour ($2 billion).
The 13-year wait certainly fueled the frenzy, and sales, around GTA VI, but some fans craved GTA VI because of what it represents in the emerging era of AI.
Even the biggest workaholics among us – startup founders – scheduled time off to play the game, including Spiry co-founder Dima Beseda, who told TechCrunch, “I reshuffled my workload to free up time around the weekends and even booked vitamin IV drips to keep my energy up.”
Yet some players felt a sense of anticipatory nostalgia as they wiped away a layer of dust on their Xbox to play the game they’d been looking forward to since they were kids.
“We do have a view that GTA is likely to be the last game of its kind to be made this way,” Ben Feder, managing partner at TIRTA Ventures and former CEO of Rockstar parent company Take-Two Interactive, told TechCrunch.
That’s because GTA VI was created entirely without generative AI.
“We’re kind of at this technological moment where this way of developing has sort of reached its natural frontier,” Feder said. “I don’t think you can say that games like this will always be around.”
As millions of people immersed themselves in Vice City, the tech industry witnessed another long-awaited moment: Anthropic became the first major AI lab to go public. At Nasdaq HQ, Anthropic executives gathered to celebrate the Claude maker’s $81.3 billion IPO. At virtually the same moment that Anthropic broke the record for the largest IPO ever, GTA VI was also breaking records with the highest-rated and best-selling game launch of all time.
But when the Anthropic team rang the bell on Thursday, the sound also signaled the end of an era in video game development, and perhaps even in the arts at large.
The AI industry operates with efficiency as its north star. The promise of this technology is that we will be able to automate so much work that we can expand the capabilities of humanity, avoiding needless time spent tinkering with ultimately fruitless ideas. Instead, a prompt goes into an LLM, and a response is spat out.
This technological revolution exploded into the world with some soul-crushing side effects: children are inundated with mind-numbing slop on YouTube, lawyers cite nonexistent cases in court, and tech companies like Meta lay off tens of thousands of people as part of a corporate-branded “Year of Efficiency.” But against the backdrop of the AI industry’s first major IPO, Rockstar has unveiled a game that about 5,000 people labored over for more than a decade.
The final product is breathtaking, looking so lifelike that it can be hard to distinguish gameplay footage from real life. These sprawling open-world games are usually made possible by procedurally generating new landscapes and objects, but Rockstar has taken the time to painstakingly craft every detail of the world, even developing 30,000 different nonplayable characters with unique appearances and personalities.
The video game industry is already grappling with the threat of AI. Google’s Project Genie, which launched earlier this year, allows users to create and wander around 3D worlds generated from prompts to an LLM. The stock prices of several video game companies faltered around the time of Project Genie’s release, perhaps because of investors’ uncertainty about the future relevance of video game developers.
“The notion that somehow new tools would allow an individual to push a button and generate a hit, market a hit, and bring it to many millions of consumers around the world, it’s a laughable notion,” Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick said at the time. “It’s just never been the case with entertainment.”
Zelnick’s fellow tech CEOs see different future, though. On a Meta earnings call this year, CEO Mark Zuckerberg promised that, “soon, you’ll have an AI that understands you and [can] even generate great personalized content for you.”
Elon Musk even went as far as proposing that a game like GTA VI could be made with AI.
“You won’t even have to ask,” Musk wrote on X. “AI will figure what video game you’d like best.”
This is the paradox of “Grandthropic” week. GTA VI is so impressively vast and captivating because its developers could make mistakes, experiment, and rework ideas, even if that meant delaying the game (twice). GTA VI was incubated with the exact inefficiencies that investors hope AI companies like Anthropic can help eradicate.
“Plenty of fantastic art — video games and elsewhere — almost by definition has to be created slowly, and there’s something to having that kind of inefficiency around it,” Feder said. “Creative output requires deletion, right? Getting to kind of a masterpiece oftentimes requires an enormous amount of deletion. And when you’re talking about a game of the kind of complexity we’re talking about, that kind of deletion ends up being very expensive, and it is by definition not efficient.”
GTA VI reeks of its own humanity – every small detail is loaded with intention, but it’s this impressive precision that keeps the world abuzz, triggering the kind of monocultural moment that has become increasingly rare in a media landscape that revolves around highly personalized social media algorithms.
The game forces the player to slow down, which is either frustrating or genius, depending on your sense of humor. People waited more than three presidential terms for the next installment in a high-octane action franchise, only to download a 212 GB behemoth of a game in which your earliest

Our top tipster Lewis Jones, aka Jones Knows, provides his analysis and betting insight across the Premier League.
Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea, Friday 8pm, live on Sky Sports
I'm not for jumping off the Nottingham Forest bandwagon just yet.
Forest have taken just four points from their last seven Premier League games - no team has taken fewer - yet they sit sixth in the expected points table for the season.
There is a significant disconnect between performance levels and results, something that usually corrects itself over time. I'm still a firm believer that Oliver Glasner will get this talented group of players motoring up the Premier League table.
And I'm struggling to see why Chelsea should command quite so much respect from the markets.
Of the ever-present Premier League teams in 2026, only one has lost more games than Chelsea (14) and only one has conceded more goals (51).
Where has Xabi Alonso's defensive magic gone?
His invincible Bayer Leverkusen side conceded just 24 league goals across their entire title-winning campaign in 2023/24. Chelsea have shipped 20 in 11 games this season alone. There is a softness to this Chelsea team when opponents turn up the intensity and attack them directly.
Just two clean sheets in their last 27 Premier League games tells a sorry tale.
Forest have the attacking weaponry to expose those defensive deficiencies.
The 29/20 with Sky Bet for a home win makes lots of sense.

Leeds vs Coventry, Saturday 3pm
When the numbers and the theory marry up in the player fouls markets, I'm usually willing to get stuck in. And there is a lovely little match-up brewing down Leeds' right flank that Sky Bet may have underestimated.
Jayden Bogle is an all-action footballer. He's busy, aggressive and covers plenty of ground, which brings him into contact with opposition players at both ends of the pitch. That is exactly the profile of player I like to get onside in the fouls markets.
Across his last 30 games for Leeds, Bogle is averaging 1.75 fouls per 90 minutes. A solid enough starting point when assessing the 10/11 with Sky Bet for him to commit two or more fouls - but it's the opposition that really gets me excited.
Coventry's Yann Gboho is a foul-drawing maestro.

There is plenty of juice in that 10/11 considering this bet has won in four of Bogle's last five games.

The Argentine looks a walking accident at times for Manchester United, such is his desire to engage physically with opposition players. But throw him into a left-back role and his chances of falling foul of the referee increase significantly.
His natural instinct is to get tight and aggressive rather than stand off his opponent - as we saw with the foul he gave away in Sporting Lisbon that led to a penalty. That's a dangerous game to play against someone with the explosive qualities of Dango Ouattara.
The Brentford winger is developing quite the reputation as a card magnet for opposition defenders.
Since the start of the 25/25 season, Ouattara has drawn a card from an opponent every 199 minutes - that's 14 cards in total. Only Crysensio Summerville (118 mins per card) has a better strike-rate.
Those are impressive numbers and his directness with the ball should make for uncomfortable viewing for Martinez. Ouattara was responsible for getting Vitaliy Mykolenko booked in Monday's win over Everton, too.

Enter Unai Emery, who is unbeaten in 10 games away from home against newly promoted opposition with Villa.

items.text:
George Russell admits feud with Max Verstappen is 'avoidable' and 'unnecessary' ahead of Qatar Grand Prix
George Russell's long-standing feud with Max Verstappen reignited at the Las Vegas GP after the pair collided in final practice; watch the Qatar GP on Sky Sports F1 this weekend, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday
Thursday 26 November 2026 16:03, UK
George Russell says he was "amused" by Max Verstappen’s criticism of him after their feud reignited at the Las Vegas Grand Prix but admits it was "avoidable".
After colliding on track in final practice last weekend, Russell publicly criticised Verstappen following the incident. The Dutchman won the race after an intense battle between them and said afterwards that the Mercedes driver is "far below my level".
The pair have clashed several times on track in the past, most notably engaging in a remarkable war of words following an incident during qualifying at the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix where Verstappen felt Russell had pushed unreasonably hard for him to be penalised.
- Qatar GP: UK schedule and how to watch on Sky Sports
- F1 2026 Calendar | F1 2026 Standings | F1 Gossip Column
- Got the Sky Sports app? Sign up for latest F1 alerts📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream F1 with no contract 📺
Speaking on Thursday - back at the Lusail International Circuit almost exactly two years on from that incident - ahead of this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, Russell said: "At the end of the day, I guess I stand by what I said after practice.
"But he was the one who went out and won the race. I didn't and I'm sure he had a bit of a laugh about that, and that was reasonably amusing. From my side, just a new race weekend, try and focus on the driving and move on."
Russell was pressed on the saga throughout the FIA press conference and revealed he was perhaps "guilty of being just too open and honest when I speak with you guys [the media]".
"It's all avoidable at the end of the day, and it's all a bit unnecessary. It's not something I'm looking to continue. I'm not looking to have poor relationships with people. That's just not really the type of person I am," he said.
"There are lessons just to be taken away from these situations. Maybe I am just too open and honest with the media because I feel that I'm having more of an open conversation with you guys as opposed to remembering there's a camera.
"There are more people in this room than there are cameras, and I feel like I'm talking to you, but I'm not actually talking to you. I need to remind myself that I'm talking to the camera there that's broadcasting to millions of people. That's the biggest takeaway."
More to follow...
